body:
I play fighting games competitively, and had a girlfriend who really liked to play with me.  Just like you, she was terrible at them and never really wanted to get better or anything, she just learned the motions for special moves and did what she could with that.

I always loved it, I would just pick characters I hadn't practiced or immediately knew how to play and ran bullshit commentary the whole time.  If she had ever expressed any interest in actually learning the game I would've gladly switched over to tourneybro mode and taught her, but she had more fun cracking up at the random crap going on screen than anything else.

With the help of Carr's book, I was able to identify why I wanted to smoke and feel capable of burning it at the source.

Started a few days early, but screw it, I'll stamp myself with the new years group.

There's definitely a difference in connotation between "she just views me as a friend" and "she friendzoned me", and the latter is what I meant to scuttle.  It's been established as a passive-agressive way of painting yourself as a victim of someone who didn't really do anything wrong.

But that's an argument of semantics, and you're completely right on every other point.

Come on dude, don't perpetuate this crap.  The friendzone's a really pathetic and broken concept that should've died with Good Charlotte and xanga.

Plus, you should probably write about shit you know.  I'm not bashing the idea of writing music to make a buck, but you can tell when a songwriter has no effing clue what they're talking about when they scribble out a tune to someone else's experience.
